Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

appropriate adjective

fitting the person or the occasion

also proper (fitting), fitting, becoming, seemly, inappropriate, it’s not right to, it’s not done

classical

Cic. Or. 74: decēre quasi aptum esse cōnsentāneumque temporī et persōnae (Lewis & Short)

decet, decēre, decuit

impersonal verb: the thing as subject or an infinitive, the person in the accusative

it is fitting, it becomes, it is proper

Cicero’s own definition: what suits the moment and the person. Dēdecet is the opposite.

Other words

  • decōrus, decōra, decōrum — becoming, seemly, proper

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 28: est decōrus senī sermō quiētus et remissus

    As a noun, decōrum is Cicero’s word for propriety, the Greek πρέπον (Lewis & Short). It can also mean handsome, adorned (poetic).

  • convenit, convenīre, convēnit — it is fitting, it is proper

    impersonal verb, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 3.2.41 (Lewis & Short, s.v. conveniō)

    The impersonal use of conveniō, “come together”, hence “agree, suit”; convenit alone also means “agreed!” (Plaut. Cas. 2.3.54).

Examples

  • īte procul, juvenēs: mītis mihi convenit aetās: folle decet puerōs lūdere, folle senēs

    off you go, young men: a gentle age suits me; the soft ball is right for boys to play with, and for old menMart. 14.47.1–2

  • est decōrus senī sermō quiētus et remissus

    calm, relaxed talk becomes an old manCic. Sen. 28

  • haud convenit ūnā īre cum amīcā imperātōrem in viā

    it isn’t proper for a general to walk in the street with his girlfriendTer. Eun. 3.2.41 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōn decet ad mēnsam cantāre.

    It isn’t proper to sing at the table.composed

See also suitable, proper, correct.
